chunks: Therefore, (fear) Allah, (fear) Allah, O creatures of Allah!

Because the world is behaving with you in the usual way and you and the Hour are in the same rope (close to each other). As though it has come with its signs, has approached with its pleas and has made you stand in its way; and as though it has come forward with all its quakings and has settled down with its chest on the ground while the world has parted from its people and has turned them out of its lap. It was like a day that has passed or a month that has gone by. Its new things have become old and the fat ones have become thin.

They are in a narrow place, in very complicated affairs and in a fire whose pain is sharp, cries are loud, flames are rising, sound is trembling, burning is severe, abatement is remote; its fuel is burning, its threats are fearful, its hollows are hidden, its sides are dark, its vessels are aflame, and everything about it is abominable.

key_terms.السَّاعَةُ: The Hour, the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What is the description of the world and Hellfire in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) employs the rhetorical device of *isti'arah* (metaphor) to personify the world as a departing traveler, a motif deeply rooted in early Shia asceticism (*zuhd*) that underscores the urgency of spiritual preparation. This passage serves as a bridge between worldly transience and the eternal reality of the Hereafter, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on *mawt* (death) as a natural transition rather than an end. The vivid description of Hellfire's attributes aligns with classical tafsir interpretations of divine justice, urging believers to maintain vigilance (*taqwa*) amidst the chaos of worldly signs.
